A perforated screen or openwork (usually at the end of a suction pipe of a pump), used to prevent solid bodies from mixing in a liquid stream or flowline.
Debris in water that blocks the passage of solid objects.
One who strains.

wiktionary.gloss: A trans lesbian.

blocks.etymology: From un- + shrinkable.
vi_block: Không thể co lại, không thể rút ngắn lại.

wiktionary.gloss: That cannot shrink and cannot be shrunk.

examples: This cello has a terrible wolf tone on the D string.
wiktionary.gloss: An unpleasant tone produced when a note matches the natural resonating frequency of the body of a musical instrument, the quality of which may be likened to the howl of a wolf.

blocks.etymology: Borrowed from Mandarin 陰陽／阴阳 (yīnyáng), from Middle Chinese 陰陽 (MC 'im yang), from Old Chinese 陰陽 (OC *qrɯm laŋ), from 陰 (“dark” → “negative force”) + 陽 (“bright” → “positive force”).

wiktionary.gloss: Yin and yang.
A circular symbol with white and black sections (☯), representing the fusion of the concepts of yin and yang.
The vulva or vagina.

examples: He thought he could smuggle the drugs over the border by putting them in capsules and stuffing them up his yin-yang. Not a good idea!
wiktionary.gloss: The anus or rectum.
